topIssues.title: Flaky: TestInteropFaultProofs_ConsolidateValidCrossChainMessage — challenger shut down before subtests complete
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
**Claude:** Filing this flake report based on CI analysis.

## Flake Summary

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Test | `TestInteropFaultProofs_ConsolidateValidCrossChainMessage` |
| Package | `github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/proofs/serial` |
| Job | `memory-all-opn-op-geth` |
| Flakes (30d) | 3 |
| Pipeline | 119875 |

## Observed Failure

The test times out (2h) because the challenger service is stopped immediately after the subtests are launched. From CI job 4619849 logs:

```
06:17:31 — Enabling cannon-kona for super challenger
06:17:32 — challenger game service start completed
06:17:44 — RUN Consolidate-AllValid-challenger
06:17:44 — Closing challenger  ← stopped immediately after subtests start
06:17:45 — Stopped challenger game service
```

The challenger never processes any games because it's torn down before the subtests can use it. All subtests then time out waiting for challenger activity that will never happen.

## Suspected Root Cause

Race condition in test orchestration: the challenger cleanup runs concurrently with or immediately after subtest launch. The subtests need the challenger to be running, but the parent test's cleanup (or a context cancellation) shuts it down too early.

## CI Links

- Job: [4619849](https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/119908/workflows/5548eaa4-e86f-4d48-8d75-dade232b61b5/jobs/4619849)
- Branch: `aj/fix/contract-call-timeout`

topIssues.title: Remove Code skipping L2ProxyAdmin version check
topIssues.author: 0xiamflux
topIssues.body:
## Description
The ProxyAdmin contract currently lacks a `version()` function. To avoid reverts during version downgrade checks in `L2ContractsManager`, the `L2ProxyAdmin` is currently skipped. This function is planned for inclusion in a future upgrade.

This issue tracks the removal of the logic that skips the `L2ProxyAdmin` check once the `version()` function is available.

topIssues.title: Optimize Docker build workflows
topIssues.author: falcorocks
topIssues.body:
# Optimize Docker build workflows

## Summary

The GitHub Actions Docker build workflows build all images on every qualifying commit, regardless of which files actually changed. For PRs that only touch a single service, this wastes significant CI time building ~18 unaffected images. Additionally, the workflow structure leads to a confusing PR experience and maintenance burden due to duplicated configuration.

## Problems

### 1. No per-image change detection

The [`branches.yaml`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/.github/workflows/branches.yaml) workflow has coarse `paths` filters (e.g. `ops/docker/**`, `packages/contracts-bedrock/**`) but once triggered, it builds **every image** in the matrix. A PR that only modifies `op-node` code will still build `op-batcher`, `cannon`, `kona-node`, and 15 other images.

PRs should only build affected images. When a PR touches code for a single service, only that service's image should be built. Changes to shared infrastructure (the [Dockerfile](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/ops/docker/op-stack-go/Dockerfile), [`docker-bake.hcl`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/docker-bake.hcl), `ops/docker/`, etc.) should still trigger all builds. Scheduled builds should continue to build all images.

### 2. Confusing fork/local branch job visibility

The workflow uses mutually exclusive `if` conditions to split builds between [local branches](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/.github/workflows/branches.yaml#L47) and [fork PRs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/.github/workflows/branches.yaml#L91). On any given PR, one set of jobs always runs and the other is always skipped — but both sets are displayed in the GitHub checks UI. This means contributors see ~18 skipped jobs alongside ~18 running jobs, making it hard to find the actual results.

Contributors should only see relevant jobs — not a wall of skipped jobs for the build path that doesn't apply to their PR. The fork/local security model must be preserved: images built from local branches are pushed to the registry, while fork builds must never push to the registry.

### 3. Duplicated image matrix

The image list is repeated **four times** in [`branches.yaml`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/.github/workflows/branches.yaml): [`build`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/.github/workflows/branches.yaml#L51-L69), [`build-fork`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/.github/workflows/branches.yaml#L95-L113), [`check-cross-platform`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/.github/workflows/branches.yaml#L137-L154), and [`check-cross-platform-rust`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/.github/workflows/branches.yaml#L176-L178). Adding or removing an image requires updating all four locations, which is error-prone.

The set of images to build should be maintained in a single location, not duplicated across multiple jobs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] PRs that only affect a single service build only that service's image (plus any images affected by shared code changes).
- [ ] Contributors don't see skipped jobs for the other build path (fork vs. local).
- [ ] The image list is defined in a single location within the workflow configuration.
- [ ] Scheduled builds continue to build all images.
- [ ] The existing security model is preserved: fork PRs never push images to the registry.
- [ ] Builds continue to use the reusable [`factory` docker workflow](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/factory/blob/main/.github/workflows/docker.yaml).

topPRs.title: Chore/public docs migration
topPRs.author: ZakAyesh
topPRs.body:
**Description**
Migrates all content from ethereum-optimism/docs into the monorepo at docs/public-docs/. This is a verbatim move with no content edits — Mintlify remains the docs framework, just pointed at the new location. The live site at docs.optimism.io and all 500+ redirects remain unchanged. After this PR merges, we'll do the Mintlify dashboard cutover, triage open issues/PRs in the old repo, and archive ethereum-optimism/docs.

**Tests**
No automated tests for this change. Correctness will be verified manually after the Mintlify dashboard cutover by confirming docs.optimism.io resolves correctly and spot-checking a sample of redirects.

**Additional context**
This consolidation means doc updates and their corresponding code changes can be reviewed atomically in a single PR, rather than requiring separate PRs across two repos. It also places docs directly alongside the code they describe, making it easier to catch and fix stale documentation. The existing docs/ directory (audits, postmortems) is untouched.

topPRs.title: ci: add per-image change detection to Docker build workflow
topPRs.author: antonleviathan
topPRs.body:
Closes #19209

- New `.github/docker-images.json` as single source of truth for all 22 Docker images, their types, cross-platform check styles, and source paths
- `branches.yaml` rewritten with a `detect-changes` job that computes affected images via three-dot git diff, outputting dynamic JSON matrices consumed by all downstream jobs
- `compute-git-versions.sh` now reads its image list from `docker-images.json` instead of a hardcoded array (which was already out of sync)

## What changed

**Per-image change detection**: PRs now only build images whose source paths were touched. The detection has three tiers:
1. **Shared paths** (docker-bake.hcl, workflow files, etc.) ->  build all 22 images
2. **Shared Go paths** (go.mod, go.sum, op-service/, op-core/, op-chain-ops/, op-stack-go Dockerfile) → build all 16 Go images
3. **Per-image paths** (e.g. op-node/ triggers op-node, op-conductor, op-supernode) → build only affected images

Push-to-develop and scheduled builds continue building everything.

**Dynamic matrices** — all four downstream jobs (build, build-fork, check-cross-platform, check-cross-platform-rust) use `fromJson()` on the detect-changes outputs instead of hardcoded lists. Adding/removing an image is now a one-line change to `docker-images.json`.

**Gate job** — `docker-build-result` provides a stable check name for branch protection regardless of which images were in the matrix. Explicitly checks for detect-changes failure to avoid silent false-passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] PRs that only affect a single service build only that service's image (plus any images affected by shared code changes).
- [ ] Contributors don't see skipped jobs for the other build path (fork vs. local).
- [ ] The image list is defined in a single location within the workflow configuration.
- [ ] Scheduled builds continue to build all images.
- [ ] The existing security model is preserved: fork PRs never push images to the registry.
- [ ] Builds continue to use the reusable factory docker workflow.

topPRs.title: fix(op-reth): replace HashMap with sequential grouping in init store_entries
topPRs.author: dhyaniarun1993
topPRs.body:
# Description

## Problem

`HashedStoragesInit::store_entries` and `StoragesTrieInit::store_entries` grouped entries into a `HashMap<B256, Vec<…>>` before writing them to the proofs DB. The source cursor yields entries in sorted order `(address ASC, key ASC)`, but `HashMap` iteration randomises that order.

This caused silent data loss when the init process was killed(before processing the full batch) and restarted:

1.  A batch of 100K entries spans addresses A → E
2. HashMap iterates in random order, e.g. B, D, A, C, E
3. `store_hashed_storages(B, …)` → opens MDBX txn → commits
4. `store_hashed_storages(D, …)` → D → OK → commits
5. `store_hashed_storages(A, …)` → A → process dies (e.g. OOM)
6. On restart, `initial_state_anchor()` reads last key = D
7. Source cursor seeks past D, permanently skipping A and C
8. Init eventually completes, but the proof DB has missing entries
9. At query time → trie root / hash mismatch

## Fix
Replace `HashMap` grouping with sequential grouping that preserves the source cursor's sorted order. Consecutive entries with the same address are naturally grouped, and flushed in order. This guarantees on resume after partial commit, the last committed address is always the highest → no entries are skipped

# Tests

Added two regression tests using a `RecordingStore` spy that implements `OpProofsInitialStateStore` and captures the order of addresses passed to `store_hashed_storages` / `store_storage_branches`. Both tests assert:

1. Exactly one call per address
2. Calls arrive in strictly ascending address order

# Additional context

NA

# Metadata

Also contains code from https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19663 which fixes #19640

topPRs.title: fix(op-node): update pending_safe in follow-source (light CL) mode
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
## Summary
- In follow-source (light CL) mode, `pending_safe` stays stuck at genesis (block 0) while `safe` advances normally
- Root cause: `SyncStep()` returns early in follow-source mode and never reaches `RequestPendingSafeUpdate()`
- The `FollowSource()` / `followExternalRefs()` method updates `localSafe`, `safe`, and `finalized` but never touches `pendingSafe`
- Fix: add `tryUpdatePendingSafe()` call in `followExternalRefs()` so `pending_safe` tracks `local_safe`

## Impact
The batcher uses `pending_safe` (with `PREFER_LOCAL_SAFE_L2=true`) to determine what to batch. If the batcher connects to a light node sequencer with `pending_safe=0`, it thinks there's nothing to batch. This was observed on interop-v2 devnet where sequencer-2 (light node) had `pending_safe=0` while `safe=7637`.

## Test plan
- [ ] Verify light node sequencer's `pending_safe` advances with `safe` after this fix
- [ ] Verify batcher correctly batches when connected to a light node sequencer
- [ ] Run existing op-node tests

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
